findings.observed: Doctor follows artifact-parent and leaf symlinks, overwrites outside sentinels, and exits zero.
findings.minimal_reproduction: Point artifacts/graft/home/empty.env, update-check.json, or the artifacts parent at an outside sentinel and run doctor --json.
findings.expected: All adapter-owned writes stay below the real project artifact root.
findings.actual: Outside files were truncated or replaced.
findings.human_impact: Unrelated work can be corrupted by a supposedly diagnostic command.
findings.agent_impact: A green doctor can conceal an out-of-scope write.
findings.root_cause: Lexical paths, mkdir, and write_text are used without lstat/canonical containment or symlink-safe writes.
findings.proposed_fix: Reject symlinks in every owned component, use canonical containment and atomic regular-file writes, and recheck after execution.
findings.regression_test: Use outside sentinel symlinks for every owned parent/leaf and assert exit 2 plus unchanged bytes.
findings.tradeoff: Rejects users who intentionally symlink the state directory; that is appropriate for this bounded profile.

findings.observed: The external CLI and MCP child inherit arbitrary cloud, repository, package-registry, research, and synthetic secret variables.
findings.minimal_reproduction: Export SENSITIVE_RESEARCH_API_KEY and run an exact-version fake through adapter run map.
findings.expected: Only non-secret variables required for the structural operation cross the boundary.
findings.actual: The child saw the arbitrary sentinel; only eight named model keys were removed.
findings.human_impact: direnv-loaded project secrets can reach an external npm program.
findings.agent_impact: A long-lived MCP server can retain a credential-bearing environment.
findings.root_cause: Environment starts as dict(os.environ) and uses a narrow denylist.
findings.proposed_fix: Construct a minimal allowlist, isolate home/cache/temp, and never pass provider/proxy/npm/SSH control variables.
findings.regression_test: Seed arbitrary and common credential names and assert none reach fake CLI or server.
findings.tradeoff: Some user-specific subprocess configuration will no longer work implicitly; explicit bounded support is safer.

findings.observed: The required npm package @nanonets/graft@0.17.0 is not published; npm returns E404 and v0.17.0 has no release tag.
findings.expected: The exact documented artifact is retrievable and matches reviewed source.
findings.actual: Only upstream main declares 0.17.0; latest published/tagged release is 0.16.0.
findings.agent_impact: Doctor can never become ready through the public instructions.
findings.root_cause: The variant pinned an unreleased source version as if it were an npm release.
findings.proposed_fix: Use an actually published exact version with reviewed lock and source tag or disable integration.
findings.regression_test: Resolve clean-cache package metadata and install from committed lock.
findings.tradeoff: Using 0.16.0 narrows capabilities and must not imply unreviewed 0.17 behavior.

findings.observed: Broad REMAINDER forwarding admits help/version no-op successes, attached aliases, allow-partial behavior, huge result limits, and unbounded depth.
findings.minimal_reproduction: Run build --help, build -v, build -j99, ask --limit 999999 --full, or callers -dall through the adapter.
findings.expected: Every exposed operation has a closed typed schema, bounded output/cost, and semantic postcondition.
findings.actual: Inputs cross a denylist and may exit zero without the requested operation.
findings.human_impact: Misleading green evidence and uncontrolled output/cost.
findings.agent_impact: Repository text can steer an agent around intended restrictions.
findings.root_cause: A token denylist is used instead of per-command schemas.
findings.proposed_fix: Replace run passthrough with explicit bounded subcommands and validate before probing.
findings.regression_test: Parametrize aliases, unknown flags, max bounds, no-op help/version, and postconditions.
findings.tradeoff: Advanced upstream flags require a reviewed adapter change rather than immediate use.

findings.observed: Any PATH-first program whose output contains 0.17.0 is trusted and executed.
findings.minimal_reproduction: Place a fake node/graft first on PATH and emit the expected semver.
findings.expected: Execution is bound to a reviewed project-local package and lock.
findings.actual: The fake is reported ready and may write outside the project.
findings.human_impact: Version text is mistaken for dependency identity.
findings.agent_impact: A compromised or unexpected PATH defeats the trust boundary.
findings.root_cause: shutil.which plus permissive regex is the entire identity check.
findings.proposed_fix: Resolve a fixed local module path and validate lock, package name/version, realpaths, and exact version output.
findings.regression_test: PATH spoof must be ignored; modified/missing package metadata and lock hash must fail.
findings.tradeoff: Global installs no longer work through the safe adapter.

findings.observed: A relative repository symlink resolving outside the root is forwarded and read.
findings.minimal_reproduction: Pass a repo-relative symlink as an optional command directory.
findings.expected: Source inputs are fixed to the project or explicitly contained scopes.
findings.actual: Lexical traversal checks accept the outside target.
findings.human_impact: Unexpected source disclosure and broader indexing.
findings.agent_impact: A tool call can silently exceed task scope.
findings.root_cause: Argument values are classified as paths generically and never canonicalized by field semantics.
findings.proposed_fix: Remove repository positionals, force root, and canonicalize any supported scope.
findings.regression_test: Relative/absolute symlink and parent traversal sources must fail before subprocess execution.

findings.observed: Six of nine advertised commands do not reliably consume the adapter's non-default graph; map/callers/grep/blast fail and skeleton can return empty success.
findings.minimal_reproduction: Build under GRAFT_DIR through the original semantics, then run each advertised query against real 0.16 and source-built 0.17.
findings.expected: Every advertised command addresses the same project graph.
findings.actual: Only build/check/ask were functional in the isolated matrix.
findings.human_impact: Most of the advertised workflow is unusable.
findings.agent_impact: Empty or missing navigation can be mistaken for absence in source.
findings.root_cause: The wrapper relies on GRAFT_DIR instead of passing an explicit graph and repository root for each command.
findings.proposed_fix: Construct global graph-dir and project-root arguments internally and integration-test every operation with the real package.
findings.regression_test: Build once, exercise all exposed commands, and assert source-linked nonempty postconditions where applicable.
findings.tradeoff: Version-specific command construction must be reviewed at every upgrade.

findings.observed: Default fast, full, hardening, and release gates stop at Ruff formatting of the added adapter test while root template tests pass 97.
findings.minimal_reproduction: Officially render default, sync lock, and run cleanai.py gauntlet fast.
findings.expected: An optional integration does not break ordinary no-Graft gates and template tests catch render regressions.
findings.actual: All canonical profiles exit 1 before their substantive checks.
findings.human_impact: The advertised first run is broken.
findings.agent_impact: Green root tests create false confidence about generated output.
findings.root_cause: Unformatted generated test plus no render-and-fast regression in template suite.
findings.proposed_fix: Format the file and add a default rendered-project fast validation.
findings.regression_test: Exact official default render and canonical fast gate in CI/test workflow.
findings.tradeoff: End-to-end generation tests cost more time than text assertions.

findings.observed: Friction run metadata exposes expected/forbidden globs and verification commands while omitting model, client, permissions, network, caches, MCP schema cost, corrections, rework, and total context.
findings.minimal_reproduction: Run friction start and inspect .cleanai/runs/*/run.json from the same worktree.
findings.expected: Held-out oracle stays external and incomparable controls are rejected.
findings.actual: The agent can read the answer key and unlike runs can appear comparable.
findings.human_impact: Productivity conclusions can be biased or causal claims unsupported.
findings.agent_impact: Task leakage rewards oracle-reading rather than navigation quality.
findings.root_cause: A general instrumentation ledger is described as a blinded controlled-study harness.
findings.proposed_fix: Use external held-out oracles, versioned preregistration, fresh worktrees, and total-cost/result records; narrow ledger claims.
findings.regression_test: Assert agent-visible envelope omits oracle fields and comparator rejects control mismatches.
findings.tradeoff: True blinded trials require an external evaluator and more operational effort.

findings.observed: Upstream MCP adds its own instructions and broad schemas, uses different graph-root behavior, can replay upkeep writes, and lacks a tested project-owned lifecycle proxy.
findings.minimal_reproduction: Inspect upstream MCP server/instructions/tools/upkeep and compare with adapter CLI caps; original real handshake was not established.
findings.expected: MCP is a separately bounded capability with fixed context measured and clean teardown.
findings.actual: Direct server exposure bypasses adapter input/output bounds and authority wording.
findings.human_impact: Hidden writes, stale evidence, and competing instructions may be activated.
findings.agent_impact: Always-on schemas/instructions add context and can steer tool choice.
findings.root_cause: MCP is treated as a one-token CLI subcommand rather than a distinct trust boundary.
findings.proposed_fix: Disable it pending a bounded proxy with real protocol, freshness, context, cancellation, and residue tests.
findings.regression_test: No active MCP config by default; activation path unavailable until conformance suite passes.
findings.tradeoff: Users lose convenient integrated retrieval while safety/correctness is unproven.

findings.observed: The guide says keep .mcp.json uncommitted, but Git will stage it and context-audit ignores it.
findings.minimal_reproduction: Copy .mcp.json.example, run git add --dry-run .mcp.json, then context-audit --strict.
findings.expected: Optional client activation is ignored and visible to its declared audit boundary.
findings.actual: It is commit-prone while the audit reports no findings.
findings.human_impact: Collaborators may receive unintended auto-discovered configuration.
findings.agent_impact: Persistent tool context may appear without the project's context sensor noticing.
findings.root_cause: Missing ignore rule and overly narrow audit success wording.
findings.proposed_fix: Remove/disable MCP example for this release or ignore it and add explicit runtime-context accounting.
findings.regression_test: Git check-ignore and canonical context-route assertions.
findings.tradeoff: Manual activation becomes less convenient or unavailable.

findings.observed: Canonical branch/generated README, docs index, AGENTS router, and prompt index do not link the experiment; tutorial assumes a Git commit and origin/main that fresh output lacks.
findings.minimal_reproduction: Follow only canonical entrypoints in a fresh official render and run the first tutorial command.
findings.expected: A newcomer finds an optional route, prerequisites, outputs, failure recovery, and safe fallback.
findings.actual: The route is orphaned; friction start exits 2 and blast base is absent.
findings.human_impact: First-use workflow fails and terminology/output remains unexplained.
findings.agent_impact: Fresh agents cannot discover the bounded adapter from current authority routing.
findings.root_cause: Files were added without inbound navigation or fresh-render journey validation.
findings.proposed_fix: Add minimal routes, glossary/troubleshooting, Git preflight, and verified base-ref selection.
findings.regression_test: Link audit plus executable fresh-render tutorial preconditions/failure recovery.
findings.tradeoff: Adds a small persistent router line; detailed content must remain on demand.

findings.observed: Published 0.16.0 postinstall can queue install telemetry and spawn a detached flush unless CI/DO_NOT_TRACK is set before install; the original guide disables telemetry only afterward.
findings.minimal_reproduction: Inspect the packed package scripts/postinstall.mjs and telemetry gate at v0.16.0.
findings.expected: No installation or runtime telemetry/background process on the recommended path.
findings.actual: The documented global install precedes the opt-out command.
findings.human_impact: Network/telemetry choice can be made too late.
findings.agent_impact: Installation side effects are not represented in run evidence.
findings.root_cause: Global npm instructions assume runtime disable also protects install.
findings.proposed_fix: Use explicit project-local locked install with CI and DO_NOT_TRACK set before npm, preferably ignore scripts where verified.
findings.regression_test: Inspect lock/package scripts and run isolated install with filesystem/process/network controls.
findings.tradeoff: Ignore-scripts support must be narrowed to tested Node/OS native artifacts.

findings.observed: The 0.16 lock resolves 45 dependencies and 12 install-script packages; a transitive tree-sitter installer can fetch a GitHub binary outside npm lock integrity.
findings.minimal_reproduction: Generate a package-lock-only consumer and inspect hasInstallScript/transitive package scripts.
findings.expected: Optional installation is proportionate, inspectable, and reproducible.
findings.actual: Global mutable install has native/scripted transitive behavior not documented by the variant.
findings.human_impact: Large attack/maintenance surface for an optional navigation experiment.
findings.agent_impact: Setup failures and platform variance can be misclassified as project failures.
findings.root_cause: No reviewed project-local lock or installation-mode analysis.
findings.proposed_fix: Commit an isolated exact lock; use scripts-disabled install only on verified platforms; keep feature outside gates.
findings.regression_test: Clean local install, package identity, no-Graft removal, and OS/Node matrix.
findings.tradeoff: Native portability remains narrower and must be reported as unverified elsewhere.

findings.observed: Held-out explainability fixtures show duplicate-symbol, decorator/registry, computed-import, TOML entry-point, wheel-resource, and hidden-file misses.
findings.minimal_reproduction: Build fixture graph and compare ask/callers/blast results with source, tests, packaging, and gold.json.
findings.expected: Limitations are explicit and consequential claims are independently verified.
findings.actual: Ask micro precision is 0.30/recall 0.80; duplicate normalize callers are 0 precision/recall; duplicate blast misses 4/4 downstream.
findings.human_impact: Compelling graphs may omit real runtime/package behavior.
findings.agent_impact: Ranked results can narrow exploration too early and produce incomplete changes.
findings.root_cause: Static extraction and name resolution cannot model all dynamic Python or packaging semantics.
findings.proposed_fix: Require exact source reads, exhaustive rg/git fallback, tests/runtime/package checks, and explicit uncertainty; cap claims.
findings.regression_test: Retain adversarial gold fixtures and report precision/recall/false negatives on every upgrade.
findings.tradeoff: Fallback reads can erase nominal token savings; correctness takes priority.

findings.observed: Doctor mutates state, emits non-JSON on missing prerequisites, can re-probe to a contradictory ready=true report, and commands preserve no stable run record.
findings.minimal_reproduction: Run doctor --json without Graft, use a version-changing fake, and compare filesystem before/after.
findings.expected: Pure one-probe machine-readable outcomes and durable scoped evidence for every operation.
findings.actual: Errors are prose, state is written, and transient probes disagree.
findings.human_impact: Automation and reviewers cannot reliably classify readiness.
findings.agent_impact: Missing/invalid evidence may be summarized as a pass.
findings.root_cause: Environment preparation is coupled to probing and output has no versioned failure schema.
findings.proposed_fix: Make doctor pure, probe once, and emit versioned JSON PASS/FAIL/UNVERIFIED evidence.
findings.regression_test: All error classes parse as JSON; doctor produces no writes; run records bind source/graph/tool/exit.
findings.tradeoff: Evidence storage adds small ignored artifact cost.

findings.observed: Persistent context is unchanged and concise, but Graft is undiscoverable; the context audit excludes MCP schemas/config, and the Graft guide's authority order conflicts with ADR 0001.
findings.minimal_reproduction: Inventory all loading routes and compare guide hierarchy with ADR/context-audit scope.
findings.expected: One concise route, consistent authority order, and honest runtime-context boundary.
findings.actual: Zero context delta is achieved partly by orphaning the feature; active MCP can remain uncounted.
findings.human_impact: Users cannot locate or correctly rank evidence sources.
findings.agent_impact: Either no discovery or unmeasured always-on tool context.
findings.root_cause: Configuration presence was conflated with effective loaded context.
findings.proposed_fix: Add one minimal on-demand router line, align hierarchy, and measure MCP externally rather than claim audit coverage.
findings.regression_test: Context inventory delta/budget and canonical inbound-link checks.
findings.tradeoff: The root route grows slightly; product detail remains outside it.

findings.observed: Graft declares Node >=20 while Commander requires >=22.12; native parsers and LSP availability vary; macOS, Windows, ARM64, and Python 3.13 were not executed in the original checkpoint.
findings.minimal_reproduction: Inspect lock engine constraints and baseline environment matrix.
findings.expected: Support claims match independently run combinations.
findings.actual: Only Linux x86_64, Python 3.12, and isolated Node 22 fixture behavior have executable evidence.
findings.human_impact: Unsupported platforms may fail during optional setup.
findings.agent_impact: Tool unavailability can be confused with source-graph absence.
findings.root_cause: No cross-platform real-package matrix and conflicting transitive engine floor.
findings.proposed_fix: Require Node 22.12.x for the reviewed profile and mark all other native platforms UNVERIFIED.
findings.regression_test: Matrix Node/OS/package install and real operation smoke; narrow docs until run.
findings.tradeoff: Narrow verified support reduces convenience but avoids false claims.
